definition: Exponential derivatives preserve exponential structure. The natural exponential function is its own derivative; other bases introduce a logarithmic scale factor.
Logarithmic derivatives convert multiplicative structure into reciprocal rates. Domain restrictions remain essential because real logarithms require positive arguments.
Position, velocity, and acceleration are successive layers of change. Their signs and zeros describe direction, speed changes, turning, and concavity, while their units distinguish the quantities.

Differentiation rules compress repeated limit arguments into reliable structures. Each rule should be chosen from the algebraic form of the function and verified through units, graph behavior, or a numerical derivative.
Trigonometric derivatives connect periodic position with periodic rates. Angle measure must be in radians for the standard derivative formulas to hold without an additional conversion factor.
